build/container/setup-terminal.sh

Shell · Tier B

Supply two legal responses through a bounded disposable installation PTY.

Usage

Validation-container helper only; pass the compiled application executable as argument one.

Inputs

The executable path, script(1), timeout(1), and the container /bin/sh; no Python is required yet.

Side effects

Runs --setup --verbose with separate License and EULA answers; installation output remains visible and script --return preserves failure.

Cleanup

timeout bounds setup to one hour and a thirty-second kill grace; installed files remain in the disposable container.

@see build/container/validate.sh

build/container/validate.sh

Shell · Tier B

Qualify extracted binaries using their newly provisioned private Python.

Usage

Run inside the fresh validation image with an artifact directory.

Inputs

Candidate smto-server or smto-gateway, /validation storage and /validation-cache; model preflight is disabled.

Side effects

Records version/help/dependency state, performs the PTY setup, then runs validate_linux.py with the sole installed Python 3.12 interpreter.

Cleanup

The Python validator owns remaining qualification; the outer Docker driver retains evidence and removes successful test installations.

@see build/tools/validate_linux.py

build/container/validation-entry.sh

Shell · Tier B

Prepare an unprivileged validation identity in a disposable container.

Usage

Container entry point only, before invoking validate.sh.

Inputs

OF_UID and OF_GID from the invoking ordinary user; the image must have no system Python.

Side effects

Creates or reuses the UID, assigns its group/home, grants container-only passwordless sudo and switches to that identity.

Cleanup

Account and sudoers changes last for the disposable container; never run this entry point on a deployment host.

@see build/container/validate.sh
